scenes.visual: close-up illustration of the edge of a closing steel lift door in an Indian apartment building, a thin black sensor strip running down the full door edge glowing with a faint warm red-orange line as the brightest thing in the frame, a person's hand reaching in from the side towards the gap, the door edge large and filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: That thin black strip on a lift door's edge? What's it actually *watching*?

scenes.visual: clean cutaway illustration of a lift door edge cut open, showing a tall column of tiny round lights inside the black strip, each tiny light glowing bright red-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, the steel door cool grey-blue, the cutaway large and centred in the lower two-thirds of the frame, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: It's a row of tiny *lights*, all shining across at the other door. And the real trick? Sneakier than a camera.
scenes.headline: STEP 1/3: TINY *LIGHTS*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: two lift door edges slide in, beams switch on one by one from the floor up between tiny lights and catchers, a beam counter climbs to 24
scenes.narration: And the other door has a row of *catchers*. Dozens of beams, floor to about head height. So why can't you see them?
scenes.headline: STEP 2/3: A *CURTAIN*

scenes.visual: close-up illustration of a hand pointing a black TV remote at a television in a cosy Indian living room, the small bulb at the front tip of the remote glowing bright red-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, the remote and hand large in the lower two-thirds of the frame, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Because it's *infrared*, the same invisible light your TV remote sends. So what happens when your hand gets in the way?
scenes.headline: LIKE YOUR *REMOTE*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a hand slides into the gap between the lift doors, the beams it covers stop arriving, the counter drops from 24 to 17, MISSING, then the doors slide back open
scenes.narration: Your hand blocks a few beams, like standing between the remote and the TV. The catchers spot the *gap*, and the doors open.
scenes.headline: STEP 3/3: A *GAP*

scenes.visual: illustration of an old-style lift door with a thick black rubber safety edge running down its side, the rubber edge glowing bright red-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, a shopping bag gently touching the rubber edge, the door edge large in the middle of the frame, nothing important in the bottom third, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Honestly, I thought it was a camera. Older lifts didn't even use light, just a rubber edge that had to *bump* you.
scenes.headline: THE OLD *WAY*

scenes.visual: warm illustration of a smiling young Indian woman stepping into a lift as the steel doors slide back open for her, the thin sensor strips on both door edges glowing bright red-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, the woman and doors large in the middle of the frame, nothing important in the bottom third, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: So the lift never really sees you. <short pause> It just notices the light that went *missing*. Next time the doors bounce back, you'll know.
scenes.headline: IT NEVER *SEES* YOU

youtube.title: Why do lift doors reopen? Invisible beams #shorts
youtube.description:
Why do lift doors reopen when your hand gets in the way? That thin black strip on the door edge is a row of tiny infrared lights, shining across at a row of catchers on the other door: dozens of invisible beams, from near the floor to about head height. That's how elevator doors sense you. Put your hand in the gap and a few beams stop arriving, the lift door infrared sensor notices the missing light, and the doors open again. Older lifts used a rubber safety edge that had to touch you first.
